encounters.sighted.merchant.1: {ships, plural, one {A broad-bellied knarr wallows} other {# broad-bellied knarrs wallow}} on the swell, deep with cargo. {lookout} makes out the colours of {faction}.
encounters.sighted.merchant.2: Traders out of the harbours of {faction}, {ships, plural, one {one hull} other {# hulls}} low in the water. They have seen you and keep their distance.
encounters.sighted.merchant.3: A merchant sail on the horizon, steering wide of you. Her crew is some {men} men, more used to oars than spears.
encounters.sighted.merchant.4: {lookout} points to a sail. A trader of {faction}, by the cut of her: slow, heavy, and worth a look.
encounters.sighted.merchant.5: Smoke from a cook-fire on a knarr's deck. Merchants of {faction}, lying to while they mend a sheet. They watch you come with wary faces.
encounters.sighted.patrol.1: {ships, plural, one {A longship of {faction} holds} other {# longships of {faction} hold}} the water ahead, shields along the rail. The lord's men want to know your business.
encounters.sighted.patrol.2: A patrol of {faction} comes out from behind the headland and turns across your bow. Some {men} men, by the count of {lookout}.
encounters.sighted.patrol.3: Horns from the shore, then {ships, plural, one {a sail} other {# sails}}. {faction} keeps watch over these waters, and the watch has seen you.
encounters.sighted.patrol.4: Guard-ships of {faction}, {ships, plural, one {one hull} other {# hulls}}, close from windward. Their steersman raises an open hand. Not yet a threat.
encounters.sighted.raiders.1: Low hulls with no banners, oars out and sails furled. Sea-wolves, {ships, plural, one {one ship} other {# ships}} of them, and they have turned toward you.
encounters.sighted.raiders.2: {lookout} spits over the rail. Raiders, perhaps {men} men, closing fast across {hasZone, select, yes {{zone}} other {the open sea}}.
encounters.sighted.raiders.3: A single shield at a masthead, painted red. Everyone aboard knows what that means: {ships, plural, one {a raider} other {# raiders}} out of the coasts of {faction}.
encounters.sighted.raiders.4: They come out of the haze close aboard: {ships, plural, one {a lean ship} other {# lean ships}} crowded with armed men and no cargo at all.
encounters.sighted.raiders.5: Sea-wolves. {men} of them at least, {stronger, select, more {more than you have} fewer {fewer than you have} other {about as many as you}}, and hungry by the look of their hulls.
encounters.sighted.warfleet.1: A war-fleet of {faction}: {ships, plural, one {one great ship} other {# ships in line}}, shields hung, a lord's banner at the mast.
encounters.sighted.warfleet.2: {lookout} counts the sails twice. {ships, plural, one {One ship} other {# ships}} of {faction}, some {men} men, {stronger, select, more {more than you have} fewer {fewer than you have} other {as many as you}}.
encounters.sighted.warfleet.3: Drums carry over the water. {faction} has put a fleet to sea, and it is turning toward you.
encounters.sighted.warfleet.4: The banner of {faction} at the head of {ships, plural, one {a ship} other {# ships}} under oars. Whatever they are hunting, they have seen you.
encounters.sighted.outlaws.1: Woodsmoke, and the smell of horses. Outlaws are camped across the track ahead, {men} or so, and {lookout} thinks they have not seen you yet.
encounters.sighted.outlaws.2: Broken branches and fresh tracks. A band of outlaws shadows the column, waiting for a narrow place.
encounters.sighted.outlaws.3: Men in ragged furs on the ridge, bows strung. Wolf's-heads, {stronger, select, more {more of them than of you} fewer {fewer than you} other {near your own number}}.
encounters.sighted.outlaws.4: {lookout} raises a hand. Ahead the track runs between rocks, and there are men among the rocks.
encounters.sighted.landPatrol.1: Spearmen of {faction} bar the road, {men} of them. Their leader wants to know who you are and why you walk their lord's land.
encounters.sighted.landPatrol.2: A watch-party of {faction} comes down to the ford. They have seen your shields.
encounters.sighted.landPatrol.3: Men of {faction}, some {men} strong, wait at the crossroads with a horn ready.
encounters.sighted.landPatrol.4: A lord's patrol, the colours of {faction} on their shields. They do not look surprised to see you.
encounters.caught.sea.1: They run you down. Hulls grind together and a voice calls across the gap: give up your goods, or fight for them.
encounters.caught.sea.2: The chase is lost. They come alongside, spears levelled, and wait to see what you will do.
encounters.caught.sea.3: Oars snap as the hulls close. {men} men stand ready to board. Yield a share, or stand and fight.
encounters.caught.land.1: Arrows from the trees. The band is on you before the column can close up.
encounters.caught.land.2: They spring from the rocks with a shout. Your men face outward, shields up, waiting for the word.
encounters.caught.land.3: The trap closes at the ford. Fall back to the ships, or stand and fight here.

encounters.preview.hail: {hasWho, select, yes {{who} does the talking. } other {}}News from their ports, perhaps a rumour, and a little goodwill with {faction}.
encounters.preview.trade: A small deal over the gunwale. {faction} will remember fair dealing.
encounters.preview.payToll: They leave you in peace. {peaceful, select, yes {Their lord will think better of you.} other {Buying off armed men costs Renown.}}
encounters.preview.demandToll: {pct}% they hand over a share of their silver or cargo. Dread rises, and {faction} will not forget it. {kind, select, merchant {If they refuse, they run.} other {If they refuse, they fight.}}
encounters.preview.attack: A fight {kind, select, outlaws {on land} landPatrol {on land} other {at sea}}, about {pct}% to win by your reckoning. {peaceful, select, yes {They mean no harm: striking first costs Honor and the goodwill of {faction}.} other {They would do the same to you.}}
encounters.preview.evade: {pct}% to shake them off. Fail, and {peaceful, select, yes {you lose a day beating about.} other {they close with you.}}
encounters.preview.flee: Always possible. Costs morale and wears out the oarsmen. {pct, plural, =0 {They are slower than you.} other {They are faster: {pct}% they catch you.}}
encounters.preview.pass: Keep your course and let them go their way.
encounters.preview.yield: They take a share of the silver and cargo aboard, or food if there is nothing else. No blood spilled, but Renown suffers a little.
encounters.preview.fight: Fight them where you stand, about {pct}% to win by your reckoning.
encounters.preview.slipAway: {pct}% to get past unseen. {peaceful, select, yes {Fail, and they stop you for questioning.} other {Fail, and they spring an ambush.}}
encounters.preview.fallBack: Give ground toward the ships. A few men will fall or be hurt, but the party holds together.
encounters.reason.atWar: You are at war with {faction}: they will neither parley nor trade.
encounters.reason.noParley: These are not men who talk.
encounters.reason.nothingToTrade: An empty hold and an empty purse: nothing to trade.
encounters.reason.noRoom: No deal to be had: they want nothing you carry, and you cannot pay for their food.
encounters.reason.nothingToPay: Nothing aboard to pay them with.
encounters.reason.noMen: You have no fighting men with you.
encounters.reason.noBattles: No fight can be joined here.
encounters.error.noEncounter: There is no encounter to answer.
encounters.error.notAnOption: That is not one of the choices.

encounters.notify.hail.outlaws: The outlaws answer from the trees with jeers, and melt away.

encounters.notify.tollTaken: The ships of {faction} pay up: {silver, number} silver{tons, plural, =0 {} other { and # t of goods}}. Word of it will spread.
encounters.notify.refusedFled: They refuse and crowd on sail. By the time your oars are out, they are hull-down.
encounters.notify.refusedFight: They refuse. Shields come off the rails: it will be a fight.
encounters.notify.lostDay: They would not let you slip by. A day lost beating about, {rations, plural, =0 {and tempers short} other {# rations eaten for nothing}}.
encounters.notify.evaded: {hasWho, select, yes {{who} takes the steering oar and puts} other {You put}} the wind to work. By dusk they are out of sight.
encounters.notify.fled: You run before them. They do not catch you, but the oarsmen are spent and morale falls by {morale}.
encounters.notify.passed: You let them go their way.

encounters.notify.questioned: The patrol holds you a while with questions, then lets you go.
